findings.description: deliver is now async, but flush calls it without await. The returned coroutine object is always truthy, so every digest is treated as delivered, and nothing is actually sent. Lines are removed from the queue (data loss), failed is always empty, and Python emits a 'coroutine was never awaited' warning.
findings.title: Coroutine from deliver() is not awaited

findings.description: Once deliver is awaited, other tasks may call add() during the await. add() on the defaultdict can insert a new recipient key while flush iterates over sorted(self._pending). Iterating a sorted copy is safe, but self._pending[recipient] on line 42 is fine only if the key still exists. A concurrent flush could also delete the recipient key, so `del self._pending[recipient]` at line 48 could raise KeyError, and a concurrent flush could double-send the same lines.
findings.suggestion: Guard flush with an asyncio.Lock, or use self._pending.get(recipient) and pop(recipient, None) when removing the entry.
findings.title: Queue mutation during await can break iteration and drop entries
